svg.title: Where the Load-Bearing Claims Sit
svg.desc: The treatise's claims placed on a spectrum: solved (with caveats), being built, the open frontier, and outside the frame.
svg.text: Where the Load-Bearing Claims Sit
What this treatise is honest about — and where the floor is "solved with a chapter of caveats," not solved.
SOLVED — with a chapter of caveats
idempotency · sagas · outboxes · durable timers/signals · long-running suspend & resume · "exactly-once-effectively"
…which is: at-least-once delivery + idempotent receivers + a finite-window dedup store + a restart-surviving key — four real systems
"solved" the way "the database handles concurrency" is solved: true, with caveats you ignore at your peril
BEING BUILT
decision journaling · action gates · budgets · multi-agent coordination via journaled state · fresh-state verification · per-class replay semantics
the runtimes (Temporal, Restate, DBOS, Inngest, …) are converging on these — none has the full set yet
"first-class budget" is generous: today it's workflow state your code checks; the win is that it survives replay
OPEN FRONTIER
verification — the LLM judge, fallible in both directions (false fail → needless rollback; false pass → ships broken)
adaptive compensation — a model undoing a model's mistake; bounded to reversible steps, gated like a forward act, or escalated
durable execution makes the agent consistent and auditable — it does not make the agent right
OUTSIDE THE FRAME
agent composition (child workflows) · the journal as a PII/secrets/retention liability · streaming UX vs the journaled backend
human-in-the-loop richer than a boolean · the performance tax (a round-trip per step; replay of a long workflow is slow; history must be pruned)
the property has a price — a treatise that sells the property without naming the price is selling
None of this unsays the argument.
"The runtime makes up the difference" describes a research programme with a few good products in it — not a finished thing with a vendor.
